solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Esoteric sailor's call for ceasefire

parts.note: an able seaman is an AB, so a sailor's is AB'S

indicators.note: a call is something spoken, so the word for ceasefire is given as it sounds, not as spelt

parts.note: a ceasefire is a truce

explanation.surface: A sailor shouting for a truce uses an obscure, esoteric term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'call for' looks like 'demand', but it says the word for ceasefire is only heard, not spelt.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe ideas that are obscure and hard to understand except by a few insiders.

clue.text: Organism found in aged garment

parts.note: AE (short for Latin aetatis) means aged, as on gravestones
a robe is a garment

explanation.surface: Some microbe is discovered living in an old piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: AE is the abbreviation for the Latin aetatis, 'aged', seen on memorials and portraits.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a living thing, usually a microbe, that needs oxygen to live: an example of an organism.

clue.text: Fruit crush

definitions.meaning: a gourd such as a marrow or pumpkin, botanically a fruit
to press flat or squeeze hard

explanation.surface: A fruit drink or crush, as on a café menu.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the gourd family vegetable, botanically a fruit; the other is the verb meaning to press flat.

clue.text: Drink mixed in le soirée

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters of le soirée are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A cocktail is mixed at an evening party, a soirée.
explanation.walkthrough: The accent on soirée is ignored. ROSIE LEE is Cockney rhyming slang: 'Rosie Lee' rhymes with tea.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang the phrase stands for tea, a common hot beverage.

clue.text: Break spell

definitions.meaning: to break suddenly, as a twig does
a short period, as in a cold spell or cold ...

explanation.surface: Breaking a magic spell, as in a fairy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A twig can crack in two this way, and a brief sudden period of cold weather is a cold one.

clue.text: Old foyer destroyed years ago

indicators.note: destroyed means the word foyer is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An old theatre foyer was demolished many years back.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means long ago, in times past, as in 'knights of old'.

clue.text: Printed note in English also turning up in France

indicators.note: in France means placed inside the letters for France
in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: A note printed in English also appears in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reads the pieces bottom to top in this down light, giving OOTE; 'in' (the second one) is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of text printed at the bottom of a page is a note in print at the foot of it.

clue.text: Thor's strange god with neat sound in doctrine

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of Thor are rearranged

parts.note: the name Thor, the possessive adding no letter
OD is an old minced form of God, as in 'Od's bodikins'
neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: The Norse god Thor seems strange beside a bull in religious teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' turns THOR into ORTH. NEAT for cattle and OD for God are archaic words solvers meet mainly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding conventional, accepted religious beliefs is being correct or sound in matters of belief.

clue.text: Twisted in helix, nothing is produced from thin air

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of in helix are wound into a new order

parts.note: O, the shape of zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: From a twisted spiral, something is conjured out of nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twisted' is the anagram signal; the zero-shaped letter for 'nothing' ends the Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means out of nothing, describing creation without any prior material.

clue.text: Bride's outfit wasted time for philosopher

indicators.note: time wasted means time is lost, so it is taken out

parts.note: a trousseau is the clothes a bride collects for her marriage

explanation.surface: Time was wasted over a bride's outfit instead of philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasted' removes T from TROUSSEAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was the eighteenth-century Genevan thinker who wrote The Social Contract.

clue.text: Kind of dance the President initially leads from Argentina to Canada, for example

indicators.note: leads means comes in front of the rest

parts.note: Barack Obama, President when the puzzle appeared, has the initials B O
Argentina is in the south, so S
taken as written
Canada is in the north, so N

explanation.surface: The President leads a dance from Argentina to Canada, across the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: Argentina and Canada are examples of a southern and a northern country, giving S TO N. B.O. are Barack Obama's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a type of slow waltz popular in the early twentieth century, named after the American city.

clue.text: In rush returning officer's casting vote

indicators.note: In means the officer's letters go inside the other piece
returning means the word for rush is read backwards, going up the down light

parts.note: a rush is a reed, the marsh plant
the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is a detective officer's department

explanation.surface: In a hurry, the returning officer casts the deciding vote at an election count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning officer' reads as the British official who runs an election count, but 'returning' reverses the rush to DEER and 'In' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A casting vote is the one that settles a tied ballot, breaking the deadlock.

clue.text: Dog's born with an advantage

parts.note: an asset is an advantage or benefit

explanation.surface: A dog is born with a head start in life.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a short-legged hound breed with long ears, an example of a dog.

clue.text: Whether man is fragile and frivolous creature or monster …

parts.note: 'be he' is the old form for 'whether he is', he being a man
a moth is a delicate creature fluttering aimlessly

explanation.surface: A philosophical question about man: is he a delicate butterfly or a beast?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be he rich or poor' means 'whether he is rich or poor'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a huge beast named in the Book of Job, now any enormous creature or thing.

clue.text: Robed waiter's basket

definitions.meaning: a robed attendant who waits at table in the Inns of Court
a carrier slung on a bicycle or on a pack animal

explanation.surface: A waiter in robes carries a basket.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inns of Court are the London legal societies where barristers dine.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a gown-wearing table attendant at the Inns of Court; the other a carrier for a bike or donkey.

clue.text: Posh girl has a can of glue

parts.note: gel is the upper-class pronunciation of girl
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: An upper-class girl owns a can of adhesive.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the jelly-like protein used as an adhesive and binding agent, akin to glue.

clue.text: Duck's egg in place in pond

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the abbreviation for place

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O
an egg is oval, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A duck's egg found in its spot by the pond.
explanation.definitionFit: A small area of still water is a pond, which is a similar small body of water.

clue.text: Surprise in bed

parts.note: the prank in which a sheet is folded so the sleeper's legs cannot stretch out

explanation.surface: A surprise awaits someone between the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: An apple-pie bed is a schoolboy trick: the sheet is folded back so the victim cannot get their feet down.
explanation.definitionFit: The prank bed with a doubled sheet is named after this kind of folded dessert, giving the surprise in bed.

clue.text: It could be clique in medical institution

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters of clique and in might be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A clique might form among staff at a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the French word for a private hospital or clinic, a medical institution.

clue.text: Specific cape on island

parts.note: taken as written
Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: A particular headland on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Something definite and particular rather than abstract is real and tangible, so specific.

clue.text: Car in mint condition?

parts.note: the name of a Volkswagen model and also of a ring-shaped peppermint

explanation.surface: A car in perfect condition, as a seller might advertise.
explanation.walkthrough: Mint condition means as new, but here the car is also the name of a mint sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a small Volkswagen hatchback and a peppermint with a hole.

clue.text: Strange omen about archdeacon is poison

indicators.note: about means going round the archdeacon's letters
strange signals the letters of omen are rearranged

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

explanation.surface: A bad omen surrounds a cleric who is poisoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' rearranges the omen to ENOM, and 'about' wraps it round the archdeacon's title.
explanation.definitionFit: To put venom into something is to poison it, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Nursery rhyme character to visit the loo during dance

indicators.note: during means these letters come in the middle of the dance

parts.note: to bop is to dance
to pee is to urinate, a visit to the toilet

explanation.surface: A character from a children's rhyme nips to the toilet mid-dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Bo-Peep, who lost her sheep, is a figure from a well-known children's verse.

clue.text: Married woman embracing lecturer for more than a bit

indicators.note: embracing means holding the lecturer's letter inside

parts.note: a bride is a newly married woman

explanation.surface: A newlywed hugs a lecturer rather more than slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: The bit is the metal mouthpiece, which forms only part of the headgear.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse's harness for the head includes the metal mouthpiece plus straps, so it is more than that piece.

clue.text: Disembowel some followers after scripture class

indicators.note: after means the followers' letters come later

parts.note: RE, religious education, is a school scripture lesson
a sect is a group of followers

explanation.surface: Some disciples dissect something after a religious lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: Religious education is the school subject once called scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgically, the verb means to cut out part of an organ or tissue, so to remove inner parts.

clue.text: Capital fellow

parts.note: a capital fellow sounds like a splendid chap, but is a resident of the capital city

explanation.surface: Praise for a first-rate chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like old slang for excellent; here it is the UK capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: A man living in the British capital is a fellow from that capital city.

clue.text: Create unusual position

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of create are put in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: Invent an odd stance or post.
explanation.definitionFit: In ballet it is a pose in which the body is angled to the audience, a dance position.

clue.text: Regularly spoil old piece of music

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of spoil, starting with the first

explanation.surface: An old tune is routinely ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' gives SOL, the odd letters of SPOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition or passage for one performer is a piece of music for a single player.

clue.text: Heard to choose alien for unusual punishment

indicators.note: heard means the pieces are spoken and we write what that sound spells

parts.note: to pick is to choose; ET, the film's extra-terrestrial, is an alien

explanation.surface: Someone heard that an alien was selected for a strange penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: PICK and ET together sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: It was an old military penalty in which a soldier stood on one foot on a pointed stake, a rare torment.

clue.text: Being lazy, 23 down has no right to have one instead

indicators.text: has no right to have one instead
indicators.note: the right, R, is dropped and the word one put in its place

parts.note: the answer to 23 down, the horse's headgear

explanation.surface: Being idle, a bit of harness gets a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) in BRIDLE is swapped for ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an intensified form meaning extremely idle, idle to the core.

clue.text: Free former representative imprisoned by Egypt

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: imprisoned by means placed inside Egypt's letters

parts.note: ET is the international code for Egypt
an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative

explanation.surface: A former MP is freed after being jailed in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone from a duty is to release them, making them free of it.

clue.text: This is no home unless oven is included

parts.note: love is a score of nothing in tennis, so no
a nest is a home

explanation.surface: A dwelling is not a real home unless there is an oven inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The rest of the clue is a joke: the answer contains the word OVEN within it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a hideaway for lovers, a place for a romantic affair rather than a family home.
